situation:
You are the compensation analyst at HELIX POINT BIOSCIENCES, a research company that develops laboratory testing methods for hospital systems. The vice president of human resources (judge) has asked you to recommend what the company should do about the pay gap that has opened between newly hired scientists and the scientists who have been here for years.

HELIX POINT has lost work to NORTHRUN THERAPEUTICS, a newer firm that pays well above what HELIX POINT once offered. To keep filling laboratory positions, the company raised its starting salaries twice in eighteen months. A scientist hired last spring now earns within a few hundred dollars of one who has been at the bench for eight years.

Tenured scientists have said plainly that their years count for nothing. The company promised at an all-staff meeting to review pay and report back. The review is finished: it finds tenured salaries at the going rate for the region and the gap caused entirely by the raised entry rate, and it identifies a small group of senior scientists the company could not replace quickly.

One compensation pool covers the year. Raising every tenured salary would spend what is set aside for retention awards for that small group and for the next round of hiring, leaving HELIX POINT paying less than NORTHRUN for the same scientists. Spending on the small group instead leaves the wider tenured staff with nothing after being told the company was looking into it.

The vice president of human resources (judge) wants your recommendation on how to spend the pool and what to tell the staff when the review is reported back. The vice president of human resources (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the vice president of human resources (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of human resources at HELIX POINT BIOSCIENCES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the compensation analyst to recommend how the year's compensation pool should be spent now that the pay review is finished, and to tell you what the company should say to the staff when the results are reported back at the next all-staff meeting.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it is not working?
